item: the connection pool hands out the connection that was returned last, so a write that follows another reuses a warm page cache (R470, D1)
summary: The SQLite engine's pool now uses pool_use_lifo=True. First-in-first-out rotated every checkout through all connections, so each flush found a cold page cache (3,076 pages read before COMMIT, 0 of 84 flushes warm in the measurement); last-in-first-out reuses the connection just returned (2,151 to 2,322 pages in two runs, 50 to 54 of 84 flushes warm), worth up to about 0.05 s of CPU per 8-article flush on a Linux VM, an upper bound because another commit drops the cache. The collector ceiling and the slot accounting are the same (pinned by a test with one thread per slot). Not changed, by measurement: cache_size (64 MiB to 1 GiB is worth 0.09 s) and wal_autocheckpoint (1000 vs 10000 same mean hold).
